findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is missing/empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In EventManager.create(), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for events with no destination calendar when the location is Google Meet, breaking booking creation/payment confirmation flows.

findings.title: updateLocation creates calendar references from `createdEvent` instead of `updatedEvent`
findings.body: In EventManager.updateLocation(), `referencesToCreate` maps all results and reads `result.createdEvent?.id`. Calendar results returned by `updateAllCalendarEvents()` are update results and populate `updatedEvent`, not `createdEvent`. Therefore calendar references are created with empty `uid`, `meetingId`, etc., which can create invalid/duplicate booking references and break later update/cancel operations.

findings.title: updateLocation stores undefined credentialId/externalCalendarId for calendar references
findings.body: In EventManager.updateLocation(), `referencesToCreate` uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Calendar update results produced by `CalendarManager.updateEvent()` do not include `externalId` or `credentialId` (only create results do). As a result, edited-location bookings can get calendar references with null/undefined credential and external calendar IDs, causing later reschedules/cancellations to use incorrect fallback logic or fail.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents can call updateEvent with an undefined credential
findings.body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents(), when a booking reference has `credentialId`, the code tries to find the credential in memory and then in the DB. If it is not found, or if the DB credential has no app slug, `credential` remains undefined, but the code still calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` expects a valid credential and will crash or reject when accessing credential fields.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar reference
findings.body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents(), when `newBookingId` is provided, the old calendar event deletion uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference. With collective/multiple-host events there can be multiple calendar references; the remaining old calendar events are not deleted, leaving stale events on secondary host calendars after reschedule.

findings.title: Google createEvent ignores destination externalId when credentialId is absent
findings.body: GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() now selects the calendar only by matching `destinationCalendar.credentialId === credentialId`. For legacy destination calendars that have an `externalId` but no `credentialId`, no match is found and the code falls back to `primary`. Previous behavior used the stored `externalId`, so events may now be created in the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Google createEvent patch can use undefined calendarId
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(), `selectedCalendar` may be undefined when no destination calendar matches the credential. The insert call safely uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent patch call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. This can issue a Google API patch request with an undefined calendarId.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot find a calendar and may pass undefined calendarId
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent(), if `externalCalendarId` is falsy the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, i.e. it searches for `undefined`. This will not find a calendar, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined and `calendar.events.update` is called with an undefined `calendarId`, causing updates to fail when no external calendar ID is stored.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent fallback may delete from primary instead of the intended calendar
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent(), when `externalCalendarId` is absent the fallback searches destination calendars by the same absent value and then defaults to `primary`. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar and the reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, the delete request targets the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
findings.body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent() takes the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the credential for which the event is being created. In the new multiple-host flow, CalendarManager calls createEvent once per host credential; Lark will repeatedly try to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail for secondary credentials or miss the secondary host's calendar entirely.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
findings.body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent() uses only the first `destinationCalendar` entry to build `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events`. In collective events with multiple destination calendars, this means secondary host events are created against the main host's calendar ID using secondary credentials, which can fail or create events in the wrong calendar.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent can silently succeed without creating any calendar object
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent() filters the account's calendars by the first destination calendar's `externalId`. When called for a secondary host credential whose calendars do not contain that externalId, the filtered list is empty, `Promise.all([])` resolves, and the method returns a successful NewCalendarEventType even though no event was created. This silently loses calendar events for secondary hosts.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer/eventType has no destination calendar
findings.body: In handleNewBooking(), `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later collective-event merge uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when the value is null. Therefore team member calendars are ignored exactly in the case where the organizer has no destination calendar, defeating the purpose of supporting multiple host calendars.

findings.title: Organization slug condition appears inverted
findings.body: The organization creation data changed from including `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to including it when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. This reverses the previous behavior: organizations will get a slug only when team billing is enabled and no slug when billing is disabled. Unless this reversal is intentional, it will break organization slug handling for non-billing or billing environments.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation ignores resolved credential and multiple calendar references
findings.body: In handleCancelBooking(), when cancelling all remaining recurring events and a calendar reference has `credentialId`, the code resolves `calendarCredential` (possibly from DB) but then iterates only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` to delete events. It also finds only the first `_calendar` reference on each updated booking. For collective/multiple-host bookings, credentials not present on the organizer user or secondary calendar references can be missed or deleted with the wrong credential, leaving stale calendar events.

findings.title: Paid cancellation does not await calendar deletion promises
findings.body: In the paid booking cancellation branch, the code does `await apiDeletes;` where `apiDeletes` is an array of promises. Awaiting the array does not await the contained promises, so the handler can return before calendar deletions finish and the try/catch will not catch deletion failures. It should await `Promise.all` or `Promise.allSettled` on `apiDeletes`.
